tool: osv-scanner (Google) offline mode vs npm audit

versions.osv_offline_db: npm all.zip 219 MB + PyPI all.zip, downloaded 2026-10-29 from osv-vulnerabilities.storage.googleapis.com

licences.osv-scanner: Apache-2.0 (LICENSE in module root; no copyleft)

install.note: GitHub releases are blocked here, so built from source via proxy.golang.org (151 s, needs Go). Normal install is a prebuilt release binary (seconds). First offline scan also downloads the per-ecosystem OSV database (npm 219 MB, PyPI ~35 MB) into ~/.cache/osv-scalibr; re-download on each run with --download-offline-databases (it re-fetches, ~8 s extra here) or run with --offline only to use the cache.
install.windows: yes - .goreleaser.yml in the v2.7.0 module lists goos windows/amd64 (release asset osv-scanner_windows_amd64.zip); single static Go binary, no runtime deps. Not executed on Windows here (release download blocked).

fixtures: fixtures/09-osv/: node-vuln/ (package.json + real lockfile v3, 29 packages: seeded V1 lodash@4.17.20, V2 minimist@1.2.5, V3 node-fetch@2.6.6, V4 semver@7.3.7 + clean controls picocolors@1.1.1, nanoid@6.0.2, fast-glob@3.3.3); node-clean/ (6 clean pins incl. lodash@4.18.1, minimist@1.2.8, semver@7.8.5; 23 packages); py-vuln/requirements.txt (P1 requests==2.25.1, P2 pyyaml==5.3.1 + click==8.5.0, idna==3.20, urllib3==2.8.0); py-clean/requirements.txt (all current). gen-lockfiles.sh regenerates lockfiles. KEY.json lists expected ids (author's knowledge, marked expected).

baseline.what: Today: none (no vulnerability scanning) -> 0/6 by definition. Also measured the obvious free alternative npm audit (npm 10.9.4, registry bulk advisories endpoint reachable).
baseline.command: cd fixtures/09-osv/node-vuln && npm audit --json   (tuned: npm audit --audit-level=high --json)

npm_audit.recall_python: 0/2 (ENOLOCK: 'This command requires an existing lockfile' - npm audit cannot read requirements.txt)
npm_audit.tuned: --audit-level=high --json: identical findings here (all 4 are high/critical; the moderate lodash advisories are still listed inside the lodash entry but do not change the exit code)

P1: GHSA-gc5v-m9x4-r6x2/CVE-2026-25645 (each also as a PYSEC-2026-* duplicate)

candidate_tuned.config: fixtures/09-osv/tuned/osv-scanner.toml: [[IgnoredVulns]] id=GHSA-c2qf-rxjj-qqgw, ignoreUntil=2027-01-01, reason='semver ReDoS only on trusted hard-coded version strings' (osv-scanner auto-loads osv-scanner.toml next to a lockfile, or pass --config); plus --format json. Why: shows the per-advisory suppression with a documented reason and expiry, the one thing npm audit has no equivalent for (npm audit has no ignore list without a third-party wrapper like better-npm-audit).
commands: osv-scanner scan source --offline --format json --config fixtures/09-osv/tuned/osv-scanner.toml -r fixtures/09-osv/node-vuln
osv-scanner scan source --offline --format json --config fixtures/09-osv/tuned/osv-scanner.toml -r fixtures/09-osv/node-clean

runtime_s.note: slower than the default runs purely from CPU contention at that moment, not from the config

limits: api.osv.dev is blocked by this egress proxy, so only offline mode was measurable; offline mode needs ~245 MB of DB zips in ~/.cache/osv-scalibr and ~10-14 s to load the npm DB per run (npm audit: 0.5 s, no cache). On the team's own machines the online mode (no cache, faster) is the normal path.
osv-scanner built from source here (151 s, Go toolchain) because GitHub releases are blocked; the real install is a ~30 MB prebuilt binary per OS, incl. Windows amd64.
npm audit cannot read requirements.txt (ENOLOCK) - Python coverage is the only recall difference between the two tools on these fixtures.
osv-scanner on a bare requirements.txt checks only the pinned direct deps (no transitive resolution for Python); a Node lockfile is scanned fully (all 29 packages).
Python findings are double-counted in osv-scanner JSON (PYSEC-* and GHSA-* records for the same CVE); a wrapper should dedupe by alias.

Both tools flag the same 5 lodash advisories; 3 of them (2025/2026 ids) have fixes only in lodash 4.17.23+/4.18.x - i.e. advisory data is live and the controls had to be re-pinned to today's latest to stay clean.
composer.lock (their WordPress PHP themes) is supported by osv-scanner but was not fixtured or measured here.
Runtimes are from a shared 4-vCPU box with other trials running (noise of several seconds).
reason: osv-scanner offline found 6/6 seeded (Node 4/4 + Python 2/2) with 0 false positives on 11 controls, but on Node it reports exactly the same advisory set as the free, already-installed npm audit (4/4, 0 FP, 0.5 s vs 10-14 s and 79 MB binary + 245 MB DB cache). Its only measured gain is requirements.txt coverage (2/2 vs 0/2) plus a documented per-advisory ignore list; the online mode could not be measured (api.osv.dev Forbidden). Adopt `npm audit --audit-level=high --json` today at zero cost; promote osv-scanner to ADOPT only if Python (or composer.lock) dependencies are actually part of the repos that get checked.

wrapper_tests.npm-fallback py-vuln: 2 (no lockfile; npm audit cannot scan requirements.txt)

do_not_adopt_notes: osv-scanner online mode: not measured, api.osv.dev returns 403 Forbidden through the egress proxy (exit 127 after 4 retries / 20.9 s).
No gain over npm audit on Node lockfiles: identical 4/4 recall, identical 8 advisory ids, identical 0 FP; 20-30x slower in offline mode and ~325 MB footprint vs 0.
go install of the 79 MB binary took 151 s; on the team's machines use the release binary instead (GitHub releases were blocked here so that path is untested).
osv-scanner JSON double-lists Python advisories (PYSEC + GHSA); counts need dedupe by alias in any wrapper.
